orgs.doing: New 08-31: declared a NATIONAL EMERGENCY over foreign-produced grid equipment. Executive Order 14421, signed 08-26 and published in today's Federal Register, invokes IEEPA and the National Emergencies Act to prohibit acquisition, import, transfer or installation of bulk-power system electric equipment tied to a "Covered Foreign Entity" — scope covering generation turbines, large and backup generators, substation transformers, grid-connected inverters, battery energy storage, HV circuit breakers and industrial control systems, plus associated software, firmware and remote-access capability. Sec. 2(b) reaches equipment ALREADY INSTALLED, up to replacement or removal. No country or company is named: Sec. 3(b) leaves designation to implementing rules due within 120 days (2026-12-24), with recommended FAR revisions favouring US-manufactured energy infrastructure due at 180 days (2027-02-22). The order's own recitals name "the rapid growth of advanced manufacturing, data centers, artificial intelligence, and defense production" as why the threat sharpened — the state naming the AI buildout as its reason for an industrial-policy action. He said nothing about Fed independence, the administration, buybacks or the long end — checked directly against the released text. The market read it hawkishly: the curve rose with the five- year up ~9bp and the thirty-year up ~2bp, dollar +0.56%, gold -3.28%, VIX unmoved — a rate-path repricing, not a fiscal scare — on the same day Michigan year-ahead inflation expectations FELL to 4.0% from 4.2%. Also 08-27: lost decisively in court over blacklisting Anthropic, a judge finding the designation was retaliation for criticism of the administration. CENTCOM declared the Strait of Hormuz open while ~24 tankers transited against a pre-war norm of 120-130.

Foreign firms are threading the access needle rather than exiting outright: Apple confirmed (08-14) it trained a proprietary China-specific model with Alibaba's support — becoming the first foreign company Beijing has cleared to deploy its own proprietary AI model domestically — while a Reuters exclusive (08-13) found Microsoft has quietly closed 15+ branch offices/JVs in mainland China over five years without leaving outright, staying mainly to service multinationals like ByteDance. A harder edge surfaced too: China-linked hackers used an open-source AI agent for what an Israeli security firm calls the first fully autonomous end-to-end AI-run cyberattack, breaching 85+ Taiwanese government accounts (event ~08-07, reported 08-11). Separately, a US judge dismissed YMTC's Lanham Act suit against Micron over 2021-22 "China Tech Threat" messaging (08-14), ruling it protected political speech, not commercial false advertising — the 3D NAND patent fight between them continues. Standing frame unchanged: decoupling the full AI stack — domestic chips, open-weight models as soft power, capital-markets tools — now with three weeks of hard revenue/valuation evidence behind it rather than just announcements.
